title: What Does a Sharing Question Add? Auditing LLM Survey Scores for Misinformation
abstract: arXiv:2604.06820v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Evaluating misinformation requires distinguishing whether readers believe content from whether they would share it. Asking large language models (LLMs) both questions yields two scores, but does the sharing answer contribute information beyond the credibility answer? We audit eight model versions on 290 synthetic misinformation articles, using 1,256 paired survey responses with 317 participant identifiers as an external validity criterion. An initial reversal motivates the audit: every model's raw sharing score predicts mean human sharing less accurately than its credibility score. This ordering changes after offset correction, so it does not by itself diagnose missing information. We instead distinguish score reconstructability, persistence across elicitation formats, and incremental human validity. translated_title: 分享问题能带来什么？审计大语言模型虚假信息调查评分
translated_abstract: 评估虚假信息需要区分读者是否相信内容以及他们是否会分享内容。向大语言模型（LLM）同时提出这两个问题会得到两个分数，但分享意愿的答案是否在可信度答案之外提供了额外信息？我们在290篇合成虚假信息文章上对八个模型版本进行了审计，使用1,256份配对调查回复（含317位参与者标识符）作为外部效度标准。一个初始的反转现象引发了本次审计：所有模型的原始分享分数对人类平均分享行为的预测准确性都低于其可信度分数。但经过偏移校正后这一排序发生改变，因此该现象本身并不能诊断出缺失的信息。我们转而从分数可重构性、跨引导格式的持久性以及增量人类效度三个维度加以区分。相对于留出的常数基线，可信度分数预测了模型分享变异的30.8%–72.5%；剩余的分享差异…
tldr: 该论文提出一个多维度审计框架，通过分数可重构性、跨引导格式持久性和增量人类效度三个维度，检验八个大语言模型在虚假信息调查中“分享意愿”评分是否在“可信度”评分之外具有额外信息价值，并发现仅凭原始分数排序无法做出判断。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a multi-dimensional audit framework—based on score reconstructability, persistence across elicitation formats, and incremental human validity—to determine whether LLM sharing scores add information beyond credibility scores in misinformation surveys, showing that raw score ordering alone is insufficient for this judgment.
